stemMd: Why would records of both rainfall and overflow be useful?

options.label: B
options.textMd: They eliminate the need to observe the garden.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They guarantee the garden will never overflow.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They prove every month has equal rainfall.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They relate the garden’s response to the conditions it faced.

explanationMd: Overflow alone is difficult to interpret without knowing the rainfall that produced it. Recording both connects input conditions to response, allowing a more defensible performance claim. It improves evidence rather than guaranteeing future outcomes.

distractorRationale.c: Recording performance does not make capacity unlimited.
distractorRationale.b: They are themselves a systematic form of observation.
distractorRationale.d: The first-month comparison already shows variation.
